We publish to-day our latest batch of letters
from the watering places, and it will be seen
that the season is already drawing to close.
This summer has hardly been very profitable to
the watering place hotel keepers, for the pub
lie have left them severely alone, not more on
account Of the pressure of the times, perhaps,
than because of general disposition to pay of
old, long standing scores with the innkeepers
at the first convenient opportunity. We have
often before descanted upon the abuses
which run riot at watering place hotels,
and are rather rejoiced than otherwise that
the landlords have at last met their Nemesis
and discovered that though the mills of the
gods grind slowly, they crush exceedingly fine


Of the accounts Of watering place life which
we have published this year, those from Long
Branch have Of course been the most interest
ing Thther, following in the train of Mrs
President Lincoln, focked oil the fashionables
who usually lie about loose at Sharon Springs
and Lake George, dance, drink and dress to
death at Saratoga and Newport, or battle, like
hermit mermaids, at Cape May. While all
the other summer resorts were com
paratively deserted, the hotels at the Branch
were overcrowded, and bellies and beaux bask-
ed in the brilliant atmosphere of the republican
court, and shone with sublime but sOftened
spleAdOr alongside OF Mrs. Lincoln, like stars
seen through the train of comet. Mrs. Lin
coin has now gone to Niagara--which is not ex-
ofIu N Oh ;u
bly, great deal Of water there-but she has
left so much of her influence behind her that the
hotels at Long Branch have decided to keep
open for at least another month.


1t would be interesting to know how the sum-
mer resorts down South have Jared this season,
and what proportion Of Southern ladies and
gentlemen have visited the white, red, black,
blue and green sulphur springs, and the cold,
warm and hot springs of Virginia, North Caro-
lima and Georgia; the ocean houses along the
Mexican Gulf; the Sullivan's Island of South
Carolina, which lies under the guns Of Fort
Moultrie, as Old Point Comfort does under
those of Fortress Monroe, and the Lake Pom
chartrain and Mississippi resorts, near New
Orleans. The Southern flowers, feminine and
masculine, used to bloom vary richly here at the
North during the dog days, and shed great
auriferous fragrance about them. We imagine
however, that they have had very little money
to spend, either at home or abroad, this year,
for JEFF. Davis and his forced loans have emptied
all purses and made scanty summer toilets
rather necessity than a luxury. Neverthe-
less the good hosts of the Southern hotels
must have had some visitors; and it would
be interesting to know how they treated
these angel visitants, 'tfew and far be-
tween," but still unexpected and ever
welcome gifts Of Providence. No doubt there
must have been a very small proportion of
beaux present, for most Of the young Southern.
ers have gone to the wars. We wonder if the
bellies saved time enough frem orinolne treason
and feminine espionage to~enjoy the " Lancers"
and the "Redowa." At what spring did the
Misses Scott imbibe?


Altogether, this has been losing time for
the watering place landlords all around. If they
have spent it III fasting penitence for past Of
fences, and prayer for aid in future reforma-
lions, they have done weh, and the public will
be all the more glad to meet them next year.
If not, we shall have our usual sharp stick
doubly pointed for them. and may the Provi-
dence which has deserted them this year have
mercy upon those who feel its thrust.

THE CANADIAN PRESS ON THE MAsoN1SLrDELL
CAPrURE.-We perceive that the Canadian press
still continues to make unnecessary buster
about the arrest Of Mason and Slidell. The
fact is that most of these Canadian journals are
directly hostile to the government of the United
States in this struggle against rebellion, and
they make the capture of the rebel ENJOYS
pretext for showering their abuse upon the
federal government, and making as much bad
blood out of the matter as possible. They re-
semble pack of dogs yelping and barking and
making oil the noise they can at the sight of a
stranger, till they are silenced by a word from
their master. When they hear how much more
moderately the English press discusses the
event about which they are SO clamorous, they
will stink away with suppressed growl. Those
who have the least authority for talking big and
threateningly are usually the very people who
sound the loudest trumpet. AS neighbors, if
not friends, the journals of Canada ought to
have some regard for truth, reason and decency
in their discussions, and not allow their pas
sions to run entirely away with their prudence.

The SOUTHERN PAPERS ON THE ARREST OF
MASON AND SLIDELI.-We have received intelli-
gence from the South which shows that the
news of the arrest Of Mason and Slidell had
reached the rebels, and that while it has evil
IDENTIFY fallen as bombshell in their midst, they
console themselves with the belief that il will
bring England into the conflict, and that with
her aid they will be enabled to extort their
independence in very brief time. They pro-
badly feel that their situation has now grown
so desperate that only foreign aid can save
their cause from speedy annihilation; and the
jubilant expression of their opinion that Eng
land is soon to become their ally only indicates
their wishes, and not any well founded rational
basis for such an expectation The insurgent
chiefs will probably be disappointed in this just
as much as they have been in other matters
upon which they have confidently built, delud-
ing both their followers and themselves, till
they have been awakened to the sad reality of
their situation by the memorable logic of stub
born facts.

The review near Washington yesterday was the
fgrandest that ever took place on this continent.
and will rank well with many that have graced the
celebrations Of European monarchs Seven divi-
sions of troops, embracing all arms Of the service
and about seventy thousand men, were reviewed
by General Mcclellan and staff, accompanied by
the President and Cabinet, the diplomatic corps,
de-, all of whom were mounted. The youthful
general was escorted by his body guard (Major
Barker's dragoons) and two regiments of regular
cavalry-in all, nearly two thousand mounted men,
The salute was fired from fifteen batteries of ar
tilery-about hundred guns-and the whole was
witnessed by between twenty and thirty thousand
spectators. Such brilliant spectacle may, per.
haps, never again be witnessed by the present
generation.


The North Carolina news is very important. A
smart engagement took place at Hatteras Inlet on
the l4th between the Coast Survey steamer Cor
win and the rebel steamer Curlew. The latter
vessel apparently got the worst of the contest and
retreated after receiving few minutes hot and
telling fire from the former.


The Provisional State government for North Caro-.
lima the establishment of which has been contem
plated for months, was formally instituted on the
18th inst by convention of delegates and proxies
representing fortyfve counties of the State. Ordi
nances were passed acknowledging the consttu.
tion Of the United States; appointing Marble Nash
Taylor provisional Governor of North Carolina:
proclaiming the secession act illegal and of no
force or effect, and empowering the new Cover.
nor to order special elections for representatives
to the federal Congress.


The news from the Eastern shore of Virginia
Accomac and Northampton counties-is very
cheering The advance of General Dix and the
distribution of his proclamation appears to give
almost general satisfaction. The rebels, 5000 in
number, have disbanded, and the Union men have
gained courage. The "Stars and Bars" have been
lowered and the glorious "Stars and Stripes" have
taken their place, and the residents of those coun
ties have welcomed the advance Of the Union
troops a harbinger of returning peace and pros
perity.


The tidings from the South via Louisville and
Fortress Monroe are interesting, as by it we learn
something of the disposition of the rebel troops in
Virginia, which has been constituted into mill
tary department. General Lee has left Virginia
for South Carolina. The Memphis appeal con-
firms the intelligence that the bridges of the
Tennessee and Virginia Railroad have been de.
stroyed, and adds that " two of the bridges were
costly and cannot be speedily rebuilt" Skirmishes
are taking place between the Unionists and
rebels in Tennessee, and Colonel Anderson.
rebel politician Of that State, was killed
on election day at the polls. Newspaper at
tacks are being made in the Richmond
papers against Beauregard, who published card
requesting his friends not to notice them. The
controversy is being carried on with great spirit
bitterness and anger. The intelligence of the
arrest Of Mason and Slidell caused great excite
ment among the rebels, who rejoiced in the pros.
pect Of retaliation by England. The news from
Button, s. c., confirms the report that the federal
troops had occupied Pinckney Island. The report
circulated, via New Orleans, that Generals Price
and McCulloch had completely routed the federal
army including General Fremont's body guard, at
Springfield, Missouri, certainly is important espe-
Cially when we consider the movements made bv
our troops in that neighborhood.

In THE AUTUMN os 1847, venerable old gen.
tleman. bald, with thin silvery locks falling
smoothly round his head, sat in a box of the
old Park Theater, accompanied by two young
ladies. The first act was over, and barely had

tleman arose in a box little way off from

voice shouted Ladies and gentlemen, 1 an
nounce to you the presence of Hon. John Quin-
cy Adams, ex-President Of the United States. "

hearty cheers greeted the patriot, statesman,
and sage. At the instant, too, the orchestrs
ceased their usual theater airs, and gave in
glorious style, o. Hail Columbia" yankee
Doodle" and the ''Star Spangled Banner" in
rapid succession. The audience remained
standing until the last note had died away

serene modesty which ever dwells with true
grestness-by low, graceful bow, and without
the utterance of a responsive word The ex.
President sat out the whole play. The next
session Of Congress witnessed the close Of his
memorablelife.
